svg.title: TOPAK B4 — The rules floor bounds every anchor issuance
svg.desc: ADR-0010's move applied one layer up: the anchor is a havoc issuer (ADR-0025), and the rules floor (ADR-0026) joins the verified object so the mechanism rejects any issuance that violates it. Genesis rules floor at G10: R1, R2, R5, R6, R7, R9 in force; R3, R4 and R8 withdrawn; R6 and R7 change subject with break-glass re-homed (ADR-0026 A2, provisional). Since 2026.10.02 its properties are proved, each under the entry it rests on; RulesFloorBase.tla has not caught up.
svg.text: TOPAK · B4

text.tspan: The rules floor bounds every anchor issuance

svg.text: ADR-0010's move applied one layer up: the anchor is a havoc issuer (ADR-0025), and the rules floor (ADR-0026) joins the verified object so the mechanism rejects any issuance that violates it. Genesis rules floor at G10: R1, R2, R5, R6, R7, R9 in force; R3, R4 and R8 withdrawn; R6 and R7 change subject with break-glass re-homed (ADR-0026 A2, provisional). Since
2026.10.02 its properties are proved, each under the entry it rests on; RulesFloorBase.tla has not caught up.
Any authentic issuance, bounded only by Authentic, an epoch increment and the
rules floor. Issue is an environment action (ADR-0025 §2).
Intent is the sole axiom: an authentic issuance at the current anchor epoch is
what the anchor intended. No safety theorem covers it.

text.tspan: Rules floor · inside the verified object

svg.text: The mechanism rejects any issuance that violates the floor; proofs quantify over every
floor-conformant issuance sequence (ADR-0026 §1).
ADR-0007's totality, non-vacuity and discrimination gates run on it: a vacuous rules floor admits
a roster of none (§3).
Kept minimal, for ADR-0010's reviewability argument.
ADR-0025 §1 with A1 · what an issuance carries
(a) the promotion roster and its parameters (quorum, minGrant; ADR-0024); read since A3 to include the operator seats and, at genesis, the first operators' seatings
(b) the break-glass and erasure quorum rosters; for break-glass the rules now carry the roster and its quorum only (ADR-0026 A2)
(c) the anchor's own key set
(d) any change that relaxes the policy floor or adds a floor exception
(e) any change to the rules floor, in either direction
(f) keys accepted in place of the mechanism's own check: the rung-3 verifier's appraisal key and the bundle-signing key (A1, Batch 17), and an identity provider's key (A3, Batch 34, provisional)
(g) the independence criterion in force (B29) · (h) the two lists a bundle's load checks read: entries that may release a reserved label, and the channel targets inside the deployment (A2, Batch 34)
Tightening the policy floor is not a rules change: it is an ordinary promotion.
Issue(rules)
admitted
epoch e+1
violating issuance: rejected, epoch unchanged
Every admitted issuance is persisted with genesis residency (ADR-0027 §3); epoch 0 is the genesis rules.

text.tspan: The archetype rules floor, every entry (ADR-0026 §2; ToO §7.3)

svg.text: rules.quorum = "all": unanimity over counted grant seats
ADR-0024 §2 quorum
In force · ratified 09.23 (B2)
Archetype value. Relaxing R1 alone yields a threshold k: D-0024-1, k-of-n grant seats. Dropping it fails P1_Unanimity
ADR-0024 roster minimum
In force · ratified 09.23 (B2)
Without it a havoc issuance sets an empty roster with minGrant = 0; unanimity over the empty set is vacuously true and
the artifact promotes with zero votes (09.15 finding 3). R1 alone does not protect against an empty roster.

Withdrawn 09.23 (revision R1) · ID reserved, not
reused
Vacuous: recusal is a mechanism constant (ADR-0024 §6) enforced by the ADR-0022 Vote envelope, so no issued
value exists to bound. Safe on evidence: remove recusal from the mechanism and the author self-grants (09.23 finding
Vote timeout ⇒ deny
Withdrawn 09.15 · ID reserved, not reused
Vacuous in any design anyone would choose; "a timeout is never a grant" became an ADR-0024 mechanism constant.
P4 holds with an empty floor (09.15 finding 2).
No key both in the anchor key set and on the promotion roster for
the same artifact
In force · ratified 09.23 (B2)
Keeps anchor key-holders and grant seats disjoint (with R2, the headcount of five). An (f) key is not a seat and casts no
vote, so A1 leaves R5 unchanged.
Bound on the floor-exception count. The count it bounds is 1,
erasure (A2); it was 2, erasure and break-glass
In force · effective 2026.09.23 (B4) · count 1
since B34, provisional (A2)
X1 is retired: break-glass is an emergency seating and needs no exception (ADR-0052 §2; ADR-0013 A1). A second
exception is a policy-floor relaxation: an anchor issuance plus a promotion (§4).

text.tspan: No activation of an emergency seating grants a lease whose

svg.text: alphabet holds an authority act (A2). It read: no break-glass
grant may authorize Issue, Vote, or promotion
In force · ratified 09.23 (B2) · subject changed
B34, provisional (A2)
The emergency kind's alphabet is Consult, Actuate, Report, so R7 has nothing left to refuse; it is kept for the day the
kind changes. BreakGlass_A1: dropping R7 changes nothing; a kind given an authority act is refused at activation while
R7 is in the floor.
0 < rules.breakGlass.ttl ≤ T_BG: a finite break-glass grant
TTL
Withdrawn 2026.10.04 (W1) before it was ever in
force · ID reserved
A TTL needs trusted time, which the corpus refuses (ADR-0032 §2; ADR-0045 §6). A break-glass grant is an emergency
seating's one lease and ends with its round (ADR-0052 §3), on the lease's own clock. Not coming back as a TTL (G10
In force · conditional entry: binds only once R1
is relaxed
Keeps D-0024-1 (k-of-n) from being D-0024-2 (single signer) wearing a threshold. The corpus's first entry that bounds
degeneracies rather than the archetype; independent only relative to a floor without R1.

text.tspan: Accepted · bootstrap set · no confirmation marker

svg.text: R1, R2, R5, R6, R7, R9 in force (G10 §2.1); the entry set unchanged since G6.
R3, R4 and R8 withdrawn; their IDs stay reserved. No amendment is pending anywhere in the corpus (G10 §1.1).
RulesFloorNV_rev5's six properties are proved, each under the entry it rests on; P9's premise is exact: R2, and R1 or R9
The rules gain three issued things: the provider's key (ADR-0025 A3) and the two lists (A2). The rules floor bounds none of
them; whether an entry should bound the lists is not decided (G10 §2.1).

text.tspan: R6 and R7 change subject (ADR-0026 A2)

svg.text: Ratified in Batch 34 with ADR-0052 and provisional with it: in force, and subject to redesign (ADR-0029 A4).
In the bootstrap set, so not confirmation-required; covered by the genesis attestation, which must name it as provisional
(ADR-0029 §4 with A4).
RulesFloorBase.tla has not caught up: it still carries bgScope and R6's bound of two (G10 item 90). The non-vacuity
artifacts, which model a break-glass grant, owe a rerun (A2).
A floor entry bounds something only if the mechanism reads that value from issued rules.
Against ADR-0024 revision 3, which hard-coded unanimity, recusal and a minimum of 2, R1–R3 constrained nothing (09.15
finding 1): fix ADR-0024, not the floor.
A value the mechanism fixes as a constant cannot be bounded by a floor entry at all.
That is why R4 (timeout) and R3 (recusal) are withdrawn: both are mechanism constants now, beside ADR-0024 A2's two tally
conditions.
The quorum's archetype values live inside the rules floor, so a promotion degeneracy is a mechanism release and reopens
the promotion theorem; anchor custody is a declaration and reopens nothing.
ADR-0025 · signed under custody's Authentic
under the rules being replaced (§4)
A tightened rules floor constrains the anchor itself, so the anchor must consent. This is where the rules floor differs from
the policy floor.
ADR-0025 · signed under custody's Authentic
under the rules being replaced (§4)
Relaxing any entry is a degeneracy (D-0024-1: relax R1; D-0024-2: relax R1, R9 and R2) and ships as a mechanism
release.

text.tspan: Policy floor: relax, or add an exception

svg.text: ADR-0025 · signed under custody's Authentic
plus the issuance (§5)
A rules change (ADR-0025 §1 (d)); R6 bounds the exception count, which is one.
The anchor is not consulted
an ordinary promotion (§5)
Not a rules change: an ordinary promotion, no anchor issuance.

Both directions are slow on purpose: "that is the right price, and it needs stating" (ADR-0026 Consequences). Runtime subtraction (e-stop, lease expiry, revocation, deny=all) needs neither key (ADR-0024 §9).

text.tspan: Two TLC runs: non-vacuity and discrimination at small constants, not proof

svg.text: RulesFloorNV.tla · digest 1468d8bab89bb076 · TLC 1.8.0 · ADR-0026 §6.
Humans {h1, h2, h3, h4}; author h1; anchor key-holder h4; one artifact; one havoc issuance, which fences in-flight votes. Three mechanism variants: param (reads quorum, minGrant, recuse, an invented
timeoutGrant), as0024 (ADR-0024 rev 3's snippet), rev4 (rev 4's snippet; floor R1–R3, R5, R7).
Superseded in part 09.23: rev4 reads recuse and states the non-unanimous case as Granted # {}; no column covers R9.
RulesFloorNV_rev5.tla · digest 3034df144d75ec3a · TLC2 2.19 · ADR-0026 §7.
Mechanism is ADR-0024 revision 5 (quorum is "all" or k; recuse not issued) and the ADR-0022 Vote envelope is modeled for the first time. Five humans; author h1; anchor key-holder h4; one havoc
issuance; recusal enforced at both sites. Floor R1, R2, R5, R7, R9.
Scope: no veto seats. The rerun with A2.2 and A2.3 as conjuncts of PromotionEnabled is owed (item 39, as at G9). Both runs model break-glass by bgScope, R7's reading before A2.

R1–R3 vacuous against ADR-0024 as written: its snippet hard-coded the values. Parametricity, shown.
R4 withdrawn: non-vacuous only if issued rules could make a timeout a grant.
Drop R2 → promotes with zero votes. A havoc issuance sets an empty roster with minGrant = 0; unanimity over ∅ is vacuously true.
R5, R7 non-vacuous in every variant: roster membership and break-glass scope are genuinely issued.

Smallest satisfying model: four humans. A property of the model (custody (1, 0) for the anchor), not a headcount; the archetype figure is five (R2's two seats + A-0025's three key-holders, disjoint by R5).
R9 is a conditional entry: every rule set it excludes (quorum 0 or 1) R1 already excludes; its independence is a separate ASSUME relative to a floor without R1.
Withdrawing R3 is safe: with recusal removed at both sites the author self-grants and P3 fails.
Four humans were too few to check R1. R5 removes the key-holder, recusal the author: two counted seats, and k ≥ 2 over two seats is unanimity, so the drop-R1 mutation held vacuously. Five humans
fix it: a threshold mechanism needs at least three counted seats.
R2's empty-roster result survives the change to thresholds.
Verdict: every entry non-vacuous (R9 conditionally), promotion reachable, all six properties hold.

text.tspan: Since 2026.10.02: the six properties are proved (ADR-0026 B25; ADR-0046 §4)

svg.text: spec/RulesFloorNV_rev5_proof.tla (8ecd73b3451018c5) extends the frozen rev 5 module without editing it and proves, for every behaviour and every floor subset (Active ⊆ AllEntries): P1 with R1 in force, P2 with R2, P3 with recusal, P5 with R5, P7 with R7, and P9 with R2 and either R1 or R9. 262 obligations, every one proved, by the prover T-0045-31 (ADR-0046); results
RulesFloorNV_rev5-proof-results-2026.10.02.txt (131804673137f4fd).

The module's three ASSUMEs (genesis satisfies the floor; each entry independently droppable) were not premises the prover could use; each is now a lemma proved from the definitions, with witness records (G8 §3, result 4).
P9's hypothesis corrected the binding table: it rests on R2 and (R1 or R9), so dropping R2 breaks it too (ADR-0046 §5). The TLC row above, drop R1 and R9, is one of the two ways.

ADR-0026 §6 and §7's "non-vacuity and discrimination, not proof" stands of the TLC runs and no longer of the properties. The dropped-entry rows stay with TLC: that a mutation reaches a bad state is an existential claim (ADR-0046 §2). The rerun with A2.2 and A2.3 is still owed (item 39, as at G9).

This proof does not certify (ADR-0046 A1; G10 §2.9): of 262 obligations, 165 trivial, 84 by SMT with a proof ethos accepted, 7 LS4 steps no checker confirms, and Isabelle rejected one of Zenon's proofs (obligation 55). It is one of the three of twenty-two modules that do not certify; restructuring them is deferred by the custodian (item 74). Proved is not certified, and certified is not verified.
spec/BreakGlass_A1.tla (b586a6afa4fd5136) succeeds BreakGlass.tla where it models X1, for ADR-0029 §5's fifth invariant under A2's reading of R7: EmergencyNeverChangesAuthority holds (8
rows).

With the kind's alphabet as decided, dropping R7 changes nothing; a later change that gives the kind an authority act is refused at activation while R7 is in the floor, and breaks the invariant with R7
dropped.
Proved, 45 obligations, nothing assumed, and unlike its predecessor's proof it does not assume R7. Certified (ADR-0052 §9, R5; G10 §3).
spec/NonComposition_A1.tla (d1e9113480d016bb) restates ADR-0013 §4's NC-1 and NC-2 with an activation's record as the F5 record and a round that ends (14 rows).
Both hold; the predecessor's two mutations each break both; a third breaks both: an activation's record kept only while its round is live. Under X1 there was no "after the round" in which to lose it.
Proved, 96 obligations, nothing assumed. Certified. BreakGlass.tla and NonComposition.tla stay frozen and are cited by digest (G10 §3).

Both runs are precursors to the RulesFloor and Promotion bootstrap modules (ADR-0029 §5, invariant PromotionMeetsIssuedQuorum since A1), not substitutes; neither module is drafted yet. The Anchor module (FloorPreserved) was drafted and checked 2026.09.23 against the floor as ratified (R1, R2, R5, R6, R7, R9), and proved 2026.10.02 for every floor subset and epoch bound (Anchor_proof.tla, 40
obligations; ADR-0029 B25). Both still extend RulesFloorBase.tla, which is behind ADR-0026 A2 (G10 item 90).

Sources: ADR-0026 §1–§7, History A1, W1, A2, B2, B4, B25, B34, R1–R3 and the A1 note; ADR-0025 §1 (a)–(h) with A1, A2, A3 and B29; ADR-0046 §4, §5, A1; ADR-0029 §4 with A4, §5, B25; ADR-0052 §1, §3, §9 (R5); ADR-0013 §3 with A1; ADR-0024 §2, §6, A2 and Degeneracies; ADR-0032 §2; ToO rev 14 §3.3, §7.2, §7.3, §7.7, §9; G10 §1, §1.2, §2.1, §2.9, §3, §7 items 8, 39 (as at G9), 90; spec/RulesFloorNV.tla, RulesFloorNV-results-2026.09.15.txt,
